policy_title: Invest in criminal justice and reduce court backlogs
stated: Invest £11bn in restoring the Ministry of Justice budget to repair court buildings, restore legal aid, and ensure the Criminal Bar is sufficiently funded. Recruit more judges representative of wider society to reduce court backlogs.

source.quote: The Green Party will invest £11bn in restoring the Ministry of Justice budget over the course of the next parliament. This would be used to restore legal aid budgets, to ensure that the Criminal Bar is sufficiently well funded and to repair court buildings. Elected Greens will push to recruit more judges and to ensure that they are representative of wider society.

bearing_set.reason: Reducing court backlogs, funding the Criminal Bar, and recruiting more judges directly improves justice system functioning — a core O5 indicator (charge/conviction times, court backlogs).
Restoring legal aid materially affects access to due process and fair trial rights — a strict O9 indicator — for those who cannot afford representation.
An £11bn spending commitment to MoJ is a material fiscal outlay that bears on whether it is funded or borrowed and the sustainability of the debt path.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the policy's core purpose lands on O5 (justice system), legal-aid restoration and representative judiciary on O9 (equal treatment/due process), and the £11bn price tag on O12 (public finances). No strong case for additional fundamentals — no direct labour-market, healthcare, housing, or liberty-restriction mechanism.
